item.title: Chinese bots are faster than Usain Bolt — and more from the World Humanoid Robot Games
item.summary: # Chinese bots are faster than Usain Bolt — and more from the World Humanoid Robot Games - Click here to listen to this article - Share via - Chinese humanoid robots at Beijing’s World Humanoid Robot Games broke human athletic records, including Usain Bolt’s 100-meter sprint mark and Javier Sotomayor’s high jump mark. - The Olympics-style event comes amid intensifying U.S.-China tech tensions, with Washington moving to restrict Chinese-made humanoid robots over national security concerns as Beijing dominates global production and showcases thousands of new models. BEIJING — Chinese humanoid robots broke records set by humans, including Usain Bolt’s 100-meter sprint world record, on the opening day of the Olympics-like World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, the event organizer said. More than 2,000 humanoid robots were participating in the event, the organizer said. The five-day games, now in their second year, are a spectacle demonstrating China’s rapid progress in advanced robotics as the technology race with the U.S. heats up, with 51 events and more than 1,000 competitions taking place, including running, table tennis and soccer.
